A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CAESAR, IDES and MARCH research. Their complete main texts, equations, algorithm boxes and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports theoretical guarantees, proofs and analytical MDP examples, but no original experimental, simulation or data-analysis outcomes, including in its appendices.

after.justification: V3 remains theoretical throughout the main text and appendices. Its new Figure 1 illustrates the algorithm rather than reporting empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: Algorithm 2 and Section 4.2 change the primary coarse-estimation and sampling-optimization policy set from all deterministic policies to the K target policies. This substantially changes the central sampling procedure's search space. V3 retains the all-deterministic option; the IDES loss and updates and MARCH procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or benchmarks for empirical training or evaluation. Multiple-policy evaluation and the policy-identification and multi-reward extensions remain theoretical.

E2.justification: Neither version reports experimentally evaluated baseline sets. Comparisons with Dann et al., Yin and Wang, and DualDICE concern analytical guarantees and research positioning.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental splits, evaluation metrics, training budgets or testing protocols. The revised sampling optimization is a method change, not an empirical protocol revision.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, robustness tests or error analyses. The illustrative MDP constructions in the comparison discussion and Appendix A.3 are retained mathematical examples.

E5.justification: The Median-of-Means construction, N = O(log(1/delta)) repetitions and data-splitting argument are retained in v2 Appendix A.7 and v3 Appendix A.8. No empirical seed information or uncertainty-reporting practice is introduced.

E6.justification: Neither version reports measured performance values, empirical rankings or qualitative evaluation findings. Changes to analytical sample-complexity guarantees are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: V3 adds Lemma 4.5 and Appendix A.4's approximate-optimality argument. Corollary 4.10 and Appendix A.9 replace v2 Section 5.1's O~(H^5 SA/epsilon^2) worst-case statement with O~(poly(H) S^2 A/epsilon^2) for deterministic target policies, explicitly accounting for log(K). The Cramér–Rao-based lower-bound argument is removed. The beta-distance and policy-identification proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The central high-probability evaluation guarantee and CAESAR, IDES and MARCH contributions remain. V3 qualifies the primary optimality benchmark through target-policy mixtures while retaining the broader option, and promotes the already-present beta-distance construction into the introduction's contribution list.

C2.justification: V2 Section 5.1 interprets its variance-unaware rate as matching a lower bound up to horizon dependence. V3 removes that interpretation and identifies deriving a lower bound as an open problem. It also clarifies that offline final evaluation still involves environment interaction and explains the computational tradeoff between target-policy and globally feasible mixtures.

D1.justification: Existing IDES iteration budgets, projection bounds, MARCH parameters and Median-of-Means details are retained. V3 adds no code or data access, hardware, runtime or experimental hyperparameter information; its input-list refinements restate requirements already present in the procedure.

R1.justification: V3 adds Russo and Pacchiano (2025), Li et al. (2023), and Zhang and Zanette (2023). It situates coarse estimation relative to prior multiplicative-accuracy estimates and expands the IDES–DualDICE distinctions, while retaining the main research context.

P1.justification: V3 removes the historical opening, moves and rewrites the contribution summary into introduction bullets, substantially expands Sections 4.1–4.3's explanations, and reorganizes the results and discussion. These are extensive narrative revisions, although most appendix prose is retained.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch from a single-column format to an ICML two-column layout, with reformatted and repositioned algorithm boxes and revised headers. V3 adds a full-width colored CAESAR pipeline diagram as Figure 1; v2 has no corresponding figure.

improvement.justification: V3 improves clarity and qualification of the guarantees: it adds an explicit feasible-mixture argument in Appendix A.4, accounts for log(K) in the worst-case bound, and replaces the lower-bound-matching assertion with an acknowledged open problem. The narrower default sampling optimum trades global optimality for reduced computation, with the broader option retained. These gains support a limited overall improvement while most underlying proofs remain unchanged.
